channel.title: Acme: Science Fiction and Fantasy News
channel.description: Science fiction and fantasy fandom news, publishing, conventions, and history.

item.title: Edgar Rice Burroughs trilogy edition marks his 150th anniversary
item.description: On November 2, 2026, Subterranean Press opened a limited preorder window for ERB Books' three-volume edition of The Land That Time Forgot trilogy, explicitly issued for the 150th anniversary of Edgar Rice Burroughs' birth on September 1, 1875. The authorized set separates The Land That Time Forgot, The People That Time Forgot and Out of Time's Abyss into individual leather-bound hardbacks and adds more than 100 illustrations, including over 75 newly commissioned pieces. Contributors include Mark Schultz, William Stout, Bob Eggleton, Frank Frazetta, Roy Krenkel and J. Allen St. John. A portfolio of advertising pieces, notebook pages and correspondence makes the edition as much an exercise in pulp-history preservation as a luxury reprint.

item.title: eFanzines posts a substantial November batch of current fan publications
item.description: On November 2, 2026, eFanzines added seven new issues spanning several corners of print and digital fandom: Nic Farey's This Here... #105, Leigh Edmonds' The Chatter Box #35, Dale Speirs' Opuntia #641, Perry Middlemiss and David Grigg's Two Chairs in Print #20, Christopher J. Garcia's Claims Department #94, and two issues of Garcia's Hugo-winning The Drink Tank, #466 and #467. The update is a useful snapshot of fanzine culture as a continuing practice rather than only an archival subject. It also demonstrates the site's preservation role: eFanzines, founded December 8, 2000, maintains current publications beside deep collections of historic fan writing, convention reports and scanned Worldcon material.

item.title: New Star Trek visual history arrives on the original series' 60th anniversary
item.description: Ten Speed Press will publish Star Trek: The Original Voyages: A Visual History on November 10, 2026, during the franchise's 60th-anniversary year and exactly 60 years after “The Corbomite Maneuver” first aired on November 10, 1966. Kyle Newman and Jeff Bond's 416-page book covers the original series, the animated continuation and the first six feature films through 1991. Its archival material includes production photographs, costumes, storyboards, interviews, props, filming models and convention ephemera, alongside toys, comics and magazine covers. That breadth makes the volume potentially valuable to fan historians: it treats Star Trek not only as 79 television episodes and later films, but as a culture carried forward through conventions, collecting, publishing and licensed artifacts.

item.title: DAW acquires Julie E. Czerneda's Interstellar Diplomacy for the Underqualified
item.description: On November 5, 2026, DAW announced that it had acquired world rights to Julie E. Czerneda's Interstellar Diplomacy for the Underqualified. The publisher describes the novel as “cozy-ish” science fiction about a space-phobic scientist trapped aboard a starship who discovers that he may be the galaxy's best chance against a parasitic hive mind. DAW also frames it as a story about community and hope. The deal is notable because Czerneda, a biologist by training and a member of the Canadian Science Fiction and Fantasy Hall of Fame, has spent three decades building biologically informed far-future series including Species Imperative and The Clan Chronicles. The announcement gives established space-opera readers a fresh standalone premise while placing a veteran Canadian writer in DAW's current acquisition program.

item.title: Utopiales announces its 2026 juried prize winners
item.description: The Utopiales festival in Nantes, held October 29–November 1, 2026, has posted its 2026 prize list. Claire North's Les dieux lents, published in French by Le Bélial', received the Prix Utopiales, while Romain Benassaya's Cor Serpentis won the youth award and Cyril Bonin's Karl took the comics prize. The Prix Julia Verlanger went to R. J. Barker's Les Vaisseaux d'Os, and the festival's extraordinary prize recognized the French genre reference projects NooSFere and Quarante-deux. That last honor is especially resonant for fandom historians: both volunteer-driven resources preserve bibliographic, critical and community memory beyond the commercial life of individual books. The November 1 results offer an unusually broad snapshot of French-language speculative culture across prose, young readers, comics and fan-built scholarship.

item.title: Clarion West opens the road to its 2027 virtual workshop
item.description: Clarion West's October 16, 2026 announcement has a current November time peg: applications are opening for its 2027 virtual workshop, led by Premee Mohamed. The nine-month program will run from March through November 2027, extending the Seattle institution's recent experiment with a format designed around sustained writing, critique and professional development rather than six residential weeks. Clarion West also announced 2027 flash-fiction groups with Kij Johnson from June 3 through July 3 and said its six-week summer workshop will again be virtual. For fandom and publishing readers, this is more than a class listing. Clarion West has been a major pipeline and community institution since 1971, and its continued online structure shapes who can participate, how cohorts form, and what the workshop model may become.

item.title: Archive of Our Own warns security incident could keep fanfiction site offline for weeks
item.description: The Organization for Transformative Works disclosed on October 30 that Archive of Our Own (AO3) had been taken offline after evidence of a security incident was discovered. The volunteer-run organization said its investigation was still in its early stages and expected the fanfiction archive to remain unavailable for at least two weeks, potentially as long as four. OTW said no fanworks, bookmarks or kudos had been deleted. It did not believe its user database had been stolen but could not rule out that possibility; account information may include usernames, email addresses, IP addresses and password hashes. It advised users to change passwords reused on other websites. OTW also said donation information is stored separately. A limited or read-only reopening may be possible during recovery. The shutdown is a major disruption for a central institution in online fan culture.

item.title: Norwescon reopens venue search and invites fans to help shape its future
item.description: Norwescon announced on November 2 that it has reactivated its site selection committee to examine potential convention venues across the greater Puget Sound area. Organizers say they last conducted such a review before the pandemic, and that changes in the hospitality industry make a fresh assessment worthwhile. The convention is asking attendees and other supporters to suggest venues or amenities the committee should consider, while emphasizing that it values its current hotel. The November update also seeks donations for the Shire teen space, notes that club table applications are open, and previews a Black Friday membership sale for Norwescon 49. Hotel suite requests are being accepted as well. For fans interested in how volunteer-run conventions manage long-term planning, the venue review offers a timely look at the organizational decisions behind a major regional gathering.

item.title: Philcon marks 90 years since its 1936 beginnings at November convention
item.description: Philcon will celebrate its 90th anniversary November 20–22, 2026, at the DoubleTree by Hilton in Cherry Hill, New Jersey. The Philadelphia Science Fiction Society traces the convention to 1936, making this anniversary a landmark for organized science fiction fandom. The event has generally met annually since its founding, except during World War II. This year's principal speaker is writer Charlie Jane Anders, with Donato Giancola as artist guest of honor and Sarah Pinsker as musical guest. Philcon also plans a mini-convention devoted to Eric Flint's 1632 universe, featuring Charles Gannon and other participants connected to the series. Alongside books and writing, the convention's program encompasses artwork, science, film, television, comics, gaming and costuming. The anniversary is a reminder that participatory science fiction fan culture predates many of the genre's most familiar modern institutions.
